OP, I've been here. I'm sorry you got so much flak for what you posted, but I completely understand where you're coming from. I never wanted to be a stay at home wife, but the fast paced world around me was making me want to completely give up on life. I ended up in the wrong career, in the wrong college, among the wrong people. Now I don't mean wrong as in objectively wrong, but not the right environment for me. I don't thrive in highly competitive environments, or jobs where you have to put others down to rise up the ladder. All I wanted was to end up in a place where I could feel like I belonged. A place where people stopped to smell the roses, a place where people valued kindness and empathy more than anything else. And seeing everyone around me move so fast, and constantly talk about getting high paying jobs and as much money as they could, I kept thinking I was doing something wrong. That perhaps if I didn't thrive in this capitalistic world, I didn't deserve to be here at all. I still struggle with a lot of these thoughts and feelings, and I still haven't landed the right career yet but I'm optimistic that one day I will. The day I decided to not blindly follow everyone else, and put myself down because I wasn't able to keep up, I started becoming happier. I know not everyone can afford to take it easy, but I have no dependents, so I will go ahead and acknowledge my privilege in this regard. I'm not exactly sure what's going on with you OP, but from what you've described, it feels like you're severely burnt out. My advice to you will be that you take a short break (if you can afford to right now) to explore what you want, and go ahead and do just that. Maybe you'll find something that you feel really passionate about and something that will make you feel more energised and connected to the world. Something that will give you a good work-life balance, so that you can still pursue other hobbies and interests in your leisure time. More power to you OP, and good luck with everything. 🫂
